data.title: Skľabiňa – Mačací hrádok, a Púchov fortlet reused by the Slavs
data.excerpt: Mačací hrádok south-west of Skľabiňa is an oval fortification of about 35 × 70 m on a ridge running west to east, closed on the east by a neck ditch with a widened rampart that looks like the site of a tower. The pronounced defences were built by the people of the Púchov culture, and in the Early Middle Ages the Slavs used them again, perhaps only as a refuge; a large three-edged arrowhead and half of a beaten bronze lunula pendant are among the few finds.

children.text: The fortification of the hillfort at Skľabiňa, also called Mačací hrádok, lies south-west of the village above the valley of an unnamed side stream flowing into the Sklabinský potok. It is situated on a ridge running W – E. Its summit part is relatively easily accessible from the north, but quite steep on the other sides, and therefore suitable for defence even without any building work. The hillfort is also marked on the map of the Second Military Survey of the 19th century.

The surface of the site is covered in its upper part by a dense tangle of scrub and the remains of felling, so that practically only the lower parts of the inner enclosure are accessible, and there, in turn, there is a great deal of modern rubbish from the nearby village. The hillfort is oval in shape, measuring about 35 × 70 m, and the circuit fortification is linked at about two thirds of its length by a further transverse rampart. On the east, access along the ridge is hindered by a clearly outlined neck ditch. The transverse rampart above it is widened and gives the impression that a tower existed at this spot. The rampart is highest on the northern side. The inner surface slopes towards the west. On the surface, where it was not grassed over, darker soil showed only in places, and in it settlement remains, chiefly smaller sherds. During the trial excavation the finds at the hillfort were above all the tip of a large early medieval three-edged arrowhead and half of a beaten bronze lunula pendant, which probably belongs to the Púchov occupation of the fortlet. The Late La Tène occupation is confirmed by sporadic sherds as well.

children.text: In spite of the pronounced fortification, no more marked occupation appears at the fortlet. An important insight is that this fortification, which was built by the people of the Púchov culture, was used in the Early Middle Ages by our ancestors the Slavs as well, even if perhaps only as a refuge. It is probable (as Dr Pieta states) that the distinct neck ditch with the transverse rampart were created precisely in the period of Great Moravia. The finds obtained do not permit a more precise dating.

Dr Pieta states that the hillfort at Skľabiňa completes the picture of the occupation of the north-eastern part of the Turiec Basin, through which the original long-distance route towards the valley of the Váh passed. La Tène occupation is attested in the built-up area as well as in the cadastral area of the neighbouring village of Sklabinské Podhradie. The three-edged arrowhead indicates use of the hillfort at Skľabiňa in the Early Middle Ages, probably already in the 8th–9th century. The built-up area of the present village may also have been part of the medieval complex; a hoard of iron tools and implements was found there in the past, and iron slag was recorded as well.

A charter of the 13th century repeatedly mentions the locality of Brvenné (Brveno-hradište), which on some maps lies SE of the village. According to some inhabitants the name may also be connected with the locality of Mačací zámok mentioned below.

children.text: From this part of Turiec a whole series of hillforts is known which are placed in the early medieval period, but these were mostly dated during old surveys only by means of pottery fragments that are difficult to determine. In the nearby area (at Žabokreky) a richly furnished warrior’s grave with a sword was also found in the past.
